data.title: Tesla Robotaxis Drove 705,000 km in One Week in Austin, More Than Waymo: Report
data.description:
Tesla went from driving next to no Robotaxi miles in Austin to beating Waymo’s spring weekly average in under four months, according to a new report from Physical AI Data.

At its October peak, Tesla’s fleet covered an estimated 705,000 km (438,000 miles) in a single week, about 8% more than Waymo averaged in the city from April through June.

The data was compiled and shared by former Tesla investor relations chief Martin Viecha, who now leads Physical AI Data.

How far Tesla has come in Austin

Tesla’s best week in Austin ended October 18, according to Physical AI Data. The report compares that week with Waymo’s April-to-June average of about 653,000 km (406,000 miles) a week in the city.

Waymo releases its mileage about three months after each quarter ends, so how the two fleets stacked up in October is still unclear. The report also doesn’t say how much of that distance either fleet covered with paying passengers on board.

Waymo still has a big lead across the U.S.

While Tesla led for October, Waymo still sits at roughly 10 times Tesla’s nationwide mileage using a broader view. Physical AI Data estimates Waymo drove more than 32 million km (20 million miles) across the U.S. in October, compared with about 3.5 million km (2.2 million miles) for Tesla.

Austin and Dallas accounted for about 95% of Tesla’s Robotaxi mileage as of late October. Austin did most of the driving, while Dallas was growing more slowly as it only launched there in April, and with a small fleet. Other cities, like Fort Worth, began offering rides after the period covered by the report.

How much does each Robotaxi drive?

The firm estimates Tesla’s Texas Robotaxis averaged about 160 km (100 miles) per car per day, well below what Waymo’s cars averaged in California. Physical AI Data says freeway access could do the most to increase how far each vehicle drives, while depot capacity remains a limit on how quickly fleets can expand.

Tesla needed less than four months to go from barely driving in Austin to topping Waymo’s spring weekly average there. The next test is whether it can build up mileage that quickly in other cities. As of late October, Austin and Dallas still accounted for about 95% of all the distance Tesla’s Robotaxis drove.

data.title: Chevy Bolt leads Canada’s EV rebate requests in October, Tesla Model Y tops Ontario
data.description:
Canada’s federal EV rebate program received 14,878 requests in October, with the Chevrolet Bolt once again leading the way. The Bolt accounted for 2,420 requests, or about one in every six submitted through the Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP) last month. 

According to Transport Canada data, the Tesla Model Y took second place with 1,834 requests, followed by the Chevrolet Equinox EV with 1,321. That gave Chevrolet two of the top three spots and roughly a quarter of all requests between those two models alone.

The Ford Mustang Mach-E (1,034) and Kia Niro EV (942) rounded out the top five.

Chevrolet’s showing follows a strong summer for the Bolt. In Drive Tesla’s third-quarter rebate breakdown, the Bolt led with 5,637 rebates, while the Model Y edged out the Equinox EV by just 25.

The same three models stayed at the top in October, but the gap between second and third widened to more than 500 requests. 

Tesla Model Y leads in Ontario

Ontario was a different story. The Model Y drew 1,194 of the province’s 3,860 requests, more than double the Bolt’s 537. Model Y requests rose from 862 in September in Ontario, even as the national tally for Tesla’s SUV fell from 2,376 to 1,834.

In British Columbia, Model Y requests dropped from 1,026 to 201 over the same period. The significant drop is not due to a lack of demand, but rather supply. Since Tesla now ships Model Y to Canada from Giga Berlin, delivery wait times have been extended well into 2027.

Currently, only the entry-level Model Y Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD) is eligible for the $5,000 rebate. You can check out which vehicles are eligible and use our rebate calculator here.

Federal rebate drops to $4,000 in January

Fully electric models accounted for 12,664 requests in October, about 85% of the national total. The federal rebate for eligible fully electric vehicles is currently worth up to $5,000. That drops to $4,000 on January 1, 2027.

Whether you get the $5,000 or $4,000 depends on when the dealer submits the application, so a delivery in the new year can still qualify for the 2026 amount if the dealer submits in time and it remains valid.

data.title: Tesla calls opposition to re-elect Robyn Denholm as misguided
data.description:
Tesla is urging shareholders to re-elect Board Chair Robyn Denholm after two major proxy advisers recommended voting against her, pushing back on their criticism ahead of the December 3 annual meeting, where it it is asking shareholders to re-elect Elon Musk, Denholm and JB Straubel.

In a five-page letter published Wednesday, Tesla responded to recommendations from Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis, which both advised shareholders not to support Denholm’s re-election. The company also filed the letter with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Tesla argues the recommendations are misguided and overlook the company’s financial performance and Denholm’s contributions during her time as Board Chair, a position she has held since November 2018.

To make its case, Tesla points to a total shareholder return of approximately 1,581% during her tenure, measured through November 13, 2026. The company says its market value also grew from about $60 billion to more than $1.5 trillion over the same period.

The disagreement centres on two main governance issues. Tesla says both advisers criticized the Board’s response to a majority-supported shareholder proposal on board declassification in 2025, arguing that a binding proposal should have been put forward this year.

Glass Lewis also questioned the lack of progress on Board gender diversity, according to Tesla’s letter, and placed responsibility on Denholm as the longest-serving member of the relevant committee standing for re-election.

Tesla disputes both arguments and is asking shareholders to vote FOR Denholm, Musk and Straubel, along with all other proposals on the ballot.

The annual meeting is scheduled for December 3 at 3:00 p.m. CT.

data.title: Tesla Giga Berlin manager contests defamation penalty order, triggering public trial
data.description:
Tesla’s Giga Berlin plant manager André Thierig is headed for a public trial after challenging a defamation penalty order. The case goes back to February, when Thierig accused an IG Metall representative of secretly recording a works council meeting at the factory.

According to Handelsblatt, the German court set the fine at 80 daily rates. That means the total is 80 times a daily amount based on Thierig’s income. The court issued the order without a hearing, to which Thierig objected, meaning the fine is on hold and he remains presumed innocent. The court has yet to set a trial date.

What happened at the Giga Berlin works council meeting

The dispute started in February, when a works council meeting at the Grünheide factory ended abruptly and police seized an IG Metall representative’s laptop. Thierig told employees and posted on X that the representative had recorded the meeting. Tesla filed a criminal complaint against him, and IG Metall denied the allegation. 

During their investigation, prosecutors found no recording on the laptop, eventually dropping the case against the union representative in April. Tesla maintains the meeting could have been recorded through WhatsApp in a browser without leaving traces on the device.

The company also said the allegations against Thierig unjustified and wants the court to clarify what happened.

What happens next

Tesla, Thierig and IG Metall settled the labour court dispute, but the union had also filed a separate criminal complaint against Thierig. That complaint led prosecutors to seek the penalty order. At the upcoming trial, the court could clear Thierig or set a different penalty.

The incident came ahead of the March works council election, when the Giga United slate took the largest share of the vote and support for IG Metall fell from about 39% to 31%.

data.title: Elon Musk says Tesla will ramp up Giga Shanghai production
data.description:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk says the company plans to build more cars at Giga Shanghai. Musk made the comments during a visit to the factory on Thursday, his first since 2023, during his trip to China this week for the APEC summit.

According to media outlet Yuyuan Tantian, Musk discussed Tesla’s production plans in Shenzhen with Ren Hongbin, who heads the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade. Musk pointed to China’s manufacturing strengths during the meeting. The report gave no target or timeline for the increase.

As we reported earlier this month, Tesla delivered just 8,817 vehicles to customers in mainland China in October, down 66.1% from a year earlier and the lowest monthly tally since July 2022. The low volume was partly attributed to Giga Shanghai’s production cycles which favour exports in the first month of a quarter.

That explanation is seen in the export numbers. Giga Shanghai recorded 67,829 wholesale sales in October, up 10.3% year over year. Of those, 59,012 went overseas, accounting for a record 87% of the monthly total. 

Additionally, there was a temporary factory shutdown during China’s National Day holiday in October, also contributing to the decline.

The split between domestic sales and exports has been building all year. Through October, Tesla’s retail sales in China fell 15% to 389,905 vehicles, while exports from Shanghai more than doubled to 420,984. Combined wholesale volume reached 810,889 vehicles, up 21.4% from the same period in 2025.

Giga Shanghai builds the Model 3 and Model Y and remains Tesla’s largest factory and export hub. It built 851,000 vehicles last year, accounting for 52% of Tesla’s global production. China is still Tesla’s second-largest market behind the United States, but so far this year, more Shanghai-built Teslas have gone overseas than to buyers in China.

data.title: Tesla Sends More Cybercab Order Invites Revealing Range, Charging Speed and Warranty
data.description:
Tesla has invited more people to purchase a personal-use Cybercab, with the latest round of invitations revealing some new details about the purpose-built Robotaxi.

The information, shared on X by @sa_futurist include a new “Cybercab Specs” page, along with an order screen showing an estimated December 2026 delivery in Austin, Texas.

The specs page lists an EPA estimated range of 279 miles (449 km). It also shows 123 miles (197 km) of range added in 15 minutes at a Supercharger, based on vehicle efficiency at a constant highway speed of 65 mph (105 km/h).

Other listed features include a 21-inch Center Touchscreen, 100 W USB Power Delivery and 20.1 cubic feet of storage space. The dimensions are listed as 69.0 x 55.4 x 176.2 inches.

The screenshots also provide the first look at the warranty details. The Basic Limited Vehicle Warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles, whichever comes first, while the Battery and Drive Unit Limited Warranty runs for eight years or 100,000 miles, whichever comes first, with a minimum 70% battery capacity retention.

Tesla Insurance is listed as not included, but available to buy through the app. The order screen also repeats the US$29,990 estimated purchase price, a US$299 monthly Autonomy Subscription with one month included, and a US$1,000 non-refundable deposit.

data.title: Elon Musk Reveals Starlink V2 Launch Plans and New Rooftop Cell Tower
data.description:
Elon Musk has shared new details about SpaceX’s next-generation Starlink Mobile satellites, saying Direct-to-Cell Version 2 will begin launching next year with a major increase in bandwidth.

Speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk said the new constellation could offer 40 times the bandwidth of the current Direct-to-Cell Version 1 satellites.

“We’ll be launching the SpaceX Direct-to-Cell Version 2 constellation starting next year,” Musk said. “That will, I think, have 40 times the bandwidth of the current Direct-to-Cell Version 1, some very big multiple.”

However, that figure is lower than SpaceX’s earlier claims. In October, the company said its V2 satellites would offer more than 100 times the bandwidth of its current generation.

Bringing Starlink Mobile Indoors

Musk also discussed plans to improve indoor coverage, which remains a challenge for satellite-to-phone services, and something which legacy providers say still gives them an edge over Starlink as common building materials can block signals coming from space.

To address this, SpaceX is developing a small ground-based device that could be installed on a roof, similar to a Starlink dish.

The device would use spectrum SpaceX acquired in the 800 megahertz band, with Musk suggesting it could potentially be bundled with existing Starlink terminals.

Musk said the rooftop device has already been designed and is expected to enter production next year, although he qualified that timing with “I think.”

In Canada, Rogers Satellite already uses Starlink’s direct-to-cell network to provide satellite-powered texting in areas without traditional cellular coverage.

Elon says @SpaceX will introduce a revolutionary microcell tower device for @Starlink Mobile users that you will be able to put on your roof and will help signal penetrate through thick walls. "It addresses the problem of reaching people who are in a building. ( via NYT DealBook Summit)

— Sawyer Merritt (@SawyerMerritt) November 18, 2026

data.title: Rivian sets December 9 for its next Autonomy & AI Day
data.description:
Rivian has scheduled its next Autonomy & AI Day for December 9, a year after the company used the same event to introduce Universal Hands-Free driving, an in-house AI chip, and a new in-car assistant.

According to a media advisory Rivian posted Wednesday, the event is meant to show how far its self-driving and AI work has come, and it will stream on the company’s YouTube channel.

How to watch, and who is speaking

Rivian’s event page says the stream starts at 10 a.m. PT. If you want to watch, it will be on YouTube, and you do not need a ticket. The company says the day will include talks from its leaders, product demonstrations, and a preview of what it has planned for 2027.

Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe is on the speaking list, along with chief software officer Wassym Bensaid, James Philbin, who leads Autonomy and AI, and Vidya Rajagopalan, who oversees electrical hardware.

A Point-to-Point test is already underway

Rivian has already started inviting some U.S. owners to try a Point-to-Point feature that can follow a set route with the driver still supervising, including on highways.

That early access program is limited to second-generation R1 and R2 vehicles with a paid Autonomy+ subscription in selected states, beginning with California and Florida. First-generation R1s are left out, and Rivian says owners in Canada cannot join for now.

Invites started going out in mid-October, and Rivian says it will begin emailing people who were selected in late November. Point-to-Point is due to reach that early group in late 2026, then a wider release is planned in 2027 for eligible second-generation R1 and R2 models.

data.title: Ford Ships First U.S. Made LFP Battery Cells for Fathom Prototypes
data.description:
Ford has shipped the first battery cells from its new battery plant in Michigan, with the lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells heading to Louisville Assembly Plant to power prototypes of its Fathom electric pickup.

According to Ford, the production lines at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan can produce 40 cells per minute, making them among the fastest LFP battery production lines outside China.

Ford chose LFP batteries to help lower the cost of its electric vehicles (EVs). The chemistry does not require nickel or cobalt, while the rectangular cells fit directly into the vehicle’s chassis, further reducing costs.

The US$3 billion (C$4.30 billion) battery plant began producing cells last month using technology licensed from Chinese battery manufacturer CATL.

The partnership has drawn criticism from some U.S. lawmakers and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who expressed “profound concern” over Ford’s ties to Chinese companies in a letter to CEO Jim Farley in September.

However, Ford Vice President of Advanced Development Projects Alan Clarke said licensing the technology allowed the automaker to bring LFP battery production to the U.S. more quickly.

The first battery shipments mark another manufacturing milestone for the Fathom, with Ford also recently producing more than 5,000 unicastings for the electric pickup.

Ford plans to open its battery pack plant in Marshall, Michigan, in 2027, with the report putting the expected launch of the Fathom in the fourth quarter of next year.

data.title: How to vote in Tesla’s 2026 Annual Meeting
data.description:
Tesla’s Annual Meeting is coming up on December 3, and the company has released its voting instructions.

Shareholders can vote online, by mail, by QR code, or by phone.

All of the information will be provided in the shareholder voting materials that you will receive at your confirmed address.

If you are voting online or by phone, you will need to locate the unique control number on the insert. When prompted, you will need to enter the control number to vote.

If you are voting by QR code, you simply need to scan the QR code on the information packet, which will automatically include your control number.

If you choose to vote by mail, you will need to properly mark, sign, and date the proxy form and return your vote via the provided prepaid envelope.

Tesla’s Voluntary Retail Voting Program

Tesla has also rolled out a Voluntary Retail Voting Program that allows retail investors to give Tesla a standing instruction to vote their shares at future meetings. However, this program will start after the 2026 Annual Meeting, and shareholders can and should still vote their shares at the December 3 meeting.

How to vote if you are Canadian

If you are a Canadian who holds TSLA stock, you will need to follow your specific broker’s voting instructions. It should be noted that brokers are not able to vote uninstructed shares on director elections or Tesla executive compensation. The current deadline for the Annual Meeting is December 2 at 11:59 EST, but Canadian brokerages typically have their own deadlines, so be sure to check your specific brokerage’s details ahead of the vote.
